provenance.standard: scikit-learn User Guide: Dummy estimators; Choosing the right estimator
provenance.citation: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009) The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., Springer: §2.9 Model Selection and the Bias-Variance Tradeoff, ch. 7 Model Assessment and Selection, ch. 15 Random Forests. Breiman (2001) Random Forests, Machine Learning 45(1):5-32.
provenance.pitfall: Picking one complex model before measuring hides whether it beats a simple one, or even a naive guess. With few rows, a high-variance model fits noise.
corner_cases: The dummy baseline is the floor: a model that does not beat it on the same folds learned nothing useful.
The forest's row threshold is a sprisk default; the comparison, not the threshold, should decide.
A model of a family with no heuristic yet is put forward to be compared.

verification.invariant: The kept model beats the dummy baseline on the same cross-validation folds by more than the corrected spread of their paired differences (Nadeau & Bengio 2003).
